summary: Provides a general encoding for constraints imposed by network elements in GMPLS-controlled networks, such as asymmetric switching, label range limits and non-local label assignment, so these can be advertised for path computation.

eli5.summary: A map notes that some roads cannot turn left. This defines a standard way to write down such limits.

questions: what is a gmpls connectivity matrix
what is a port label restriction
what is a label set in gmpls
subtitle: A shared binary format for saying which ports connect and which labels may be used, so optical and other GMPLS networks can plan paths.

tldr.problem: Some GMPLS technologies, such as wavelength switched optical networks, have equipment that cannot connect every input to every output and cannot always change labels, so path computation needs to know these limits link by link.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7579 defines protocol-agnostic fields for connectivity matrices, port label restrictions, link sets, available and shared backup labels, and label sets that routing and path computation protocols can carry.
tldr.outcome: It only defines encodings. Protocol-specific documents are expected to reference it and define how the fields are carried, and it makes no IANA allocation requests itself.

today: RFC 7579 is a Proposed Standard from June 2015, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the information model of RFC 7446.

sections.title: Why Constraints Need an Encoding
sections.content:
Some data-plane technologies that use a GMPLS control plane carry extra limits on switching and on label assignment. In a Wavelength Switched Optical Network (WSON), for example, the wavelength must stay the same along a path, which the RFC calls the wavelength continuity constraint. Such limits mean that label availability matters link by link during path computation and label assignment.

RFC 7579 gives efficient encodings for the information the routing and label assignment process needs. The encodings are meant for the GMPLS routing protocols OSPF and IS-IS and for the PCE Communication Protocol (PCEP), where they are nested as sub-TLVs inside TLVs. This document defines only the elements. How they nest in each protocol is left to the protocol enhancement documents.
sections.eli5: Some special networks have rules like a train that can only use certain tracks. Before planning a trip you need those rules written down in a way every planner understands.

sections.title: Switching Asymmetry and Non-Local Labels
sections.content:
The first kind of constraint is node switching asymmetry. On some network elements a signal on one input port can reach only some output ports, and on a simple multiplexer the connection between some ports is fixed. The RFC models this with a connectivity matrix, conceptually an M*m by N*n matrix: M input ports with m labels each and N output ports with n labels each. The matrix shows which input port and label could possibly connect to which output port and label. It does not describe internal blocking that depends on state.

The second kind is non-local label assignment. If a TDM node cannot do time-slot interchange, or a WSON cannot convert wavelengths, the label chosen on one link affects other links, so sharing label constraints helps path computation. Port label restrictions describe relatively static limits on which labels a port may use. More dynamic facts live in the available labels information.
sections.eli5: Some switches only connect certain doors to certain doors, and some cannot change the color of a ball as it passes through. A planner has to know both facts to choose a route.

sections.title: The Connectivity Matrix Field
sections.content:
The matrix is written compactly as a list of pairs of link sets that are mutually connected. A node may split its matrix into several sub-matrices, each identified by a MatrixID, so that no single element gets too large and updates can be incremental. Sub-matrices must be mutually exclusive: no two share the same {src port, src label, dst port, dst label}.

The field starts with Conn (4 bits): 0 means the device is fixed and 1 means it is switched, such as a ROADM or OXC. MatrixID is an 8-bit integer, and the value 0xFF is reserved for port label constraints and must not identify a connectivity matrix.

Two combinations of link set direction are permitted for each pair A and B. With A as input and B as output, any signal entering a link in A can potentially leave on a link in B. With both bidirectional, traffic can potentially flow either way between the two sets.
sections.eli5: It is a list that says which entrance doors lead to which exit doors. Big switches can split the list into smaller numbered lists so each stays short.

sections.title: Port Label Restrictions
sections.content:
The Port Label Restrictions Field says which labels may or may not be used on a link. Several fields can be combined, and the result is the union of the restrictions they express. A MatrixID of 0xFF means the restriction applies to the port as a whole. Otherwise it applies to the matching connectivity matrix. The Switching Cap and Encoding fields define the label type and the interface type the restriction applies to.

The RstType value selects one of five restrictions:

  • SIMPLE_LABEL carries a label set of the labels permitted on the port.
  • CHANNEL_COUNT carries MaxNumChannels, a 32-bit integer for the most channels usable at once.
  • LABEL_RANGE generalizes a waveband device, with a 32-bit MaxLabelRange for the widest band and a label set for the overall tuning range.
  • The combined type carries both a label set and a channel count.
  • LINK_LABEL_EXCLUSIVITY carries a link set, meaning a label may be used at most once among those ports.
sections.eli5: Imagine a parking lot that only allows certain numbered spaces, or only five cars at once, or says no two cars across these lots may share a number. Each rule has its own label.

sections.title: The Link Set Field
sections.content:
To describe groups of links efficiently, the RFC borrows the idea of a label set and defines a link set. The header holds Action (8 bits), Dir (2 bits), Format (6 bits) and Length (16 bits), followed by link identifiers.

  • Action: 0 is an inclusive list of links; 1 is an inclusive range with a start and an end identifier, where a zero means no bound. A range may be used only with unnumbered link identifiers.
  • Dir: 0 bidirectional, 1 input, 2 output.
  • Format: 0 link local identifier, 1 local interface IPv4 address, 2 local interface IPv6 address. All identifiers in one list must be of the same type.

Link local identifiers can give more compact encodings when they are assigned sensibly.
sections.eli5: Instead of naming every door one at a time, you can say doors 3 through 42, or list a few doors, and say whether you mean ones going in, going out or both.

sections.title: Available Labels and Label Sets
sections.content:
The Available Labels Field and the Shared Backup Labels Field each hold an 8-bit priority bitmap (PRI) and one label set. The leftmost bit is priority level 0, the highest, and the rightmost is level 7, the lowest. A label available at priority M MUST also be advertised at every priority N below M, and at least one level MUST be advertised. When a label is in use by an LSP of priority N, it is then advertised as available only for priorities 0 through N-1. This supports setup and preemption as in RSVP-TE.

The Label Set Field starts with a 4-bit Action, a 12-bit Num Labels and a Length. The actions are inclusive list, exclusive list, inclusive range, exclusive range and bitmap set. For ranges, Num Labels MUST be two. For lists it MUST match the number of labels. For a bitmap, each bit stands for one label starting at the base label. The bitmap is padded to a multiple of 32 bits, and unused bits SHOULD be zero and MUST be ignored.
sections.eli5: It is like a sign-up sheet for seats that also notes how important each rider is. The label set is a short way to list the free seats: name them, give a start and end, or tick boxes on a grid.

sections.title: Worked Encoding Examples
sections.content:
The appendix applies the fields to a 2-degree, 40-channel ROADM with 80 add and 80 drop ports. Port 1 is the west line side and port 2 the east line side. Input on ports 3 to 42 can connect only to the output of port 1, and the input of port 2 can connect only to the outputs of ports 3 to 42 and to the output of port 1. The ports 43 to 82 mirror this for the other direction. The RFC says this representation uses 29 32-bit words.

If the ports can be renumbered, the bidirectional symmetry lets the same matrix be written with Dir set to bidirectional. A separate example encodes seven available channels of a 40-channel C-band DWDM system with 100 GHz spacing both as a bitmap and as an inclusive list, and another shows priority flags that make one label set available only at priority 0 and another at all priorities.
sections.eli5: The examples show the rules at work on a real-looking switch with lots of plugs, so you can see how short the list becomes when you use ranges.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC says it defines protocol-independent encodings for WSON information and does not itself introduce security issues. Documents that use these encodings in protocol extensions need to consider inspection, interception, modification or spoofing of the information, and are expected to describe the security measures they need. The RFC points to a general discussion of GMPLS security in RFC 5920.

There is no IANA allocation request for the information elements defined here. Any allocations are left to the protocol-specific documents.
sections.eli5: This RFC only writes down the shape of the notes. Whoever sends the notes around must keep them safe from snoops and forgers.

fields.name: MatrixID
fields.desc: ID of the matrix; 0xFF is reserved for port label constraints.

items.label: SIMPLE_LABEL
items.desc: Labels permitted on the port or matrix.

items.label: CHANNEL_COUNT
items.desc: Maximum number of channels usable at once.

items.label: LABEL_RANGE
items.desc: Movable center label and width, like a waveband device.

items.label: SIMPLE_LABEL & CHANNEL_COUNT
items.desc: Permitted labels plus a maximum channel count.

items.label: LINK_LABEL_EXCLUSIVITY
items.desc: A label may be used at most once among the listed ports.

items.label: Inclusive List
items.desc: Num Labels MUST match the labels listed.

items.label: Inclusive Range
items.desc: Start and end label; Num Labels MUST be two.

items.label: Exclusive Range
items.desc: Start and end label excluded; Num Labels MUST be two.

items.label: Bitmap Set
items.desc: One bit per label from the base label, padded to 32 bits.
